name: Overture Fieldwork — Coffee & Counter
description: A place-based research workspace for supplier prospecting, neighborhood partnerships and field visits, with a map, shared review queues and explicit source provenance.

fieldSchema.description: A team-owned research queue for physical places. Source observations stay separate from team review, notes and next actions. Initial adapter: Overture Maps places.

fields.name: overture_id
fields.description: Source identity from Overture GERS. Never replace this with a name-based identity.

fields.name: website_available
fields.description: A website URL appears in the source; this is not a live reachability check.

fields.name: brand
fields.description: Only the brand supplied by the source. Empty does not imply independent ownership.

fields.name: operating_status
fields.description: Source operating status, not a live verification.

fields.name: confidence
fields.description: Overture confidence that a place exists; not a partner-fit, quality, or open-now score.

fields.name: review_status
fields.description: Team decision only. Imports start unreviewed; shortlisted means worth researching, not verified fit.

fields.name: research_notes
fields.description: Human or source-cited research notes. Keep assumptions and observed facts distinct.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Optional research owner; no external contact is implied.

fields.name: last_verified_at
fields.description: ISO timestamp only after an actual verification; empty on initial import.

fields.name: raw_properties
fields.description: Unmodified source properties for inspection and future re-normalization.

fields.name: research_focus
fields.description: Team-selected research purpose, not a source classification or buying-intent signal.

fields.name: visit_status
fields.description: Team-owned visit plan. Missing means no plan is recorded. Planned does not mean a venue agreed to a meeting.

fields.name: planned_visit_at
fields.description: Optional planned visit time in ISO 8601 with offset, for example 2026-11-19T10:00:00-08:00. This is an internal plan, not a booking.

fields.name: visit_notes
fields.description: Team planning or actual visit observations. Keep plans and observed facts distinct.

fields.name: verification_status
fields.description: Team check of the supplied place identity or website. Missing means not checked; checked is not a commercial qualification.

fields.name: verification_notes
fields.description: What was checked and what the evidence showed; do not infer ownership, opening hours, or purchasing intent.

fields.name: verification_source_url
fields.description: URL actually used in the team check. It does not represent an automatically verified match.

fieldSchema.operatorGuide: Coffee & Counter supports three bounded tasks: discover potential supplier prospects; research neighborhood partnerships; and plan or record field visits. A venue category is a discovery signal, not buying intent, partnership readiness or supplier fit. Source observations, live context and team judgment are distinct. Overture IDs identify source records; records from city sources are candidates until identity is supported by name and address evidence. Nearby records and transit stops are spatial context, never evidence about the venue. Existing team-owned review, notes, ownership, next-step, visit and verification fields must survive source refreshes. Only mark visited after an actual visit and checked after inspecting the stated evidence. Missing values remain unknown. Use native guarded existing-record actions; do not contact venues, enrich people, create campaigns or send outreach from this module.

tiles.title: Choose a task, then make a deliberate decision
tiles.content:
Explore places brings the map, venue list and source evidence into one workspace.

Supplier prospects: research coffee, cafe and bakery venues before proposing a relevant supply conversation.
Neighborhood partners: compare public business context while planning an event or collaboration.
Field research: confirm the basics, plan a visit and keep the observations with the place.

Use Team shortlist for selected places and Field visits for internal plans. Category, registration and proximity never prove buying intent or partner fit.

tiles.title: Your shortlist — empty until you decide
A review status that means something
tiles.content:
Unreviewed: source data only. Verify first: an important fact needs checking. Shortlisted: worth further research. Visited: your team completed a visit. Passed: your team chose to skip.

A visit plan is not a booking. A public source is an observation, not a team decision. Keep the evidence behind your next step in research or verification notes.

definition.title: Data & method
definition.description: What the source supports, what the team decides, and how the data got here.

tiles.title: A useful slice, not an exhaustive directory
tiles.content:
Coffee & Counter starts with 486 places in a bounded central San Francisco area from Overture Maps release 2026-11-18.0. The box is west -122.422, south 37.775, east -122.393, north 37.801. Twelve coffee, cafe, bakery, tea and counter-service categories are selected, with place existence confidence at least 0.80 and permanently closed source records excluded.

Unknown source operating status stays unknown. Missing brand metadata does not prove independent ownership. A listed website has not automatically been checked.

tiles.title: Keep evidence and judgment separate
tiles.content:
Overture source facts: GERS ID, release, coordinates, category, confidence and supplied URLs. The underlying provider observations may be older than the Overture release.

Live public context: a separately requested city-source response, with its own refresh time and coverage. Similar names, nearby records and shared addresses are candidate evidence, not automatic identity matches.

Team judgment: review status, purpose, notes, owner, next step, verification and visit plans. These fields are deliberately preserved during source refreshes.

tiles.title: Deliberate trade-offs
tiles.content:
Use supplier prospecting to build a focused research queue; neighborhood partnerships to understand local context; and field research to prepare a visit. Always inspect the original source before relying on a match.

Map points are source locations and may conflict with supplied addresses. Distance is a straight-line aid, not a route or walking time. No opening-hours guarantee, contact enrichment, automatic fit score, booking, route optimization or outbound campaign is provided.

tiles.title: Attribution and source links
tiles.content:
Overture Maps Foundation and its source contributors. Per-record licenses, raw properties and source metadata remain attached. The extraction bundle includes the applicable CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0 and CC0-1.0 notices.

Overture attribution: https://docs.overturemaps.org/attribution/
Foursquare notice: https://opensource.foursquare.com/places-notice-txt/
OpenStreetMap map data: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright

Public city sources retain their own attribution and terms in the source catalog. Their availability and refresh schedules are independent of this workspace.

tiles.title: Four independent public sources
tiles.content:
Nearby city registrations: SF Treasurer & Tax Collector tax-location records within 100 m. Some may be historical or refer to another business; registration does not establish current opening status.

Nearby legacy businesses: the official Legacy Business Registry within 500 m. A nearby registry location does not make the selected venue a legacy business.

Nearby Muni stops: the published SFMTA stop inventory within 400 m. This is spatial planning context, not real-time service or a walking route.

Analysis neighborhood: the SF Planning census-tract analysis grouping around the source point. It is an organizational aid, not a legal or official neighborhood designation.

Each response retains its source link and independent freshness. These sources are fetched on demand, not joined by name into the Overture record.

definition.title: Partner research queue
definition.description: Team research stages; moving a card changes review status only. No outreach.

review_status.title: Team review
review_status.description: Shortlisted means worth further research. Choose visited only after your team actually visited.

research_notes.title: Research notes
research_notes.description: Replaces the current notes. Preserve useful existing context when editing.

next_action.title: Next step
next_action.description: A specific internal research step, such as verify the address or compare the menu.

owner.title: Research owner
owner.description: Optional person on your team. Leaving this untouched preserves the current owner.

planned_visit_at.title: Local visit date and time
planned_visit_at.description: An internal plan. Confirm opening hours separately; this is not a booking.

visit_notes.title: Visit plan
visit_notes.description: Optional route, opening-hours check or things to look for. Leaving this untouched preserves current visit notes.

visit_notes.title: Visit observations
visit_notes.description: Record only what your team actually observed. This replaces the current visit notes.

verification_notes.title: What you checked
verification_notes.description: Explain the identity, address or website evidence and any mismatch. A check is not proof of supplier fit.

last_verified_at.title: Actual check date and time
last_verified_at.description: Optional actual check time. Leave this untouched if you are not recording a date.
